title: Engawa
brief: An explorable three.js retreat built as an architectural visualization, not a game — a serene ~4.5-jō tatami room whose mats are laid in the traditional pinwheel and bordered in indigo cloth, framed in pale hinoki post-and-beam with translucent washi shoji screens that turn the walls into soft lamps. A low round chabudai holds a cast-iron tea set among undyed floor cushions and one deep-indigo zabuton — the single saturated note; a recessed tokonoma alcove carries one hanging scroll and one branch and nothing else. The front screens slide open onto an engawa wood veranda under a deep eave, which steps down over a shoe-removing stone into a karesansui dry garden — raked white gravel with concentric ripples, one upright charcoal stone skirted in moss, a leaning maple bearing borrowed autumn, a stone lantern and a bamboo screen closing the world. Everything is procedural geometry with procedural CanvasTexture materials — no images, no build step. Soft diffuse northern daylight from a cool hemisphere fill plus one gentle warm key casting deep, calm PCF shadows, ACES tone-mapped. Drag to orbit and scroll to zoom (OrbitControls); tap one of four saved viewpoints (tatami room, tokonoma, veranda, garden) to glide the camera on an eased path; or press Walk for first-person WASD movement at eye height, clamped to the site. Click any element for a one-line note — tatami, shoji, tokonoma, karesansui, and the rest. Capped render loop; prefers-reduced-motion disables easing (instant cuts, no drift).
da: Wabi-sabi calm — a quiet, natural, tatami-order retreat in soft northern light: pale hinoki wood (#D8C7A6), off-white washi paper screens (#F2EDE2), tatami green-beige (#B4B27E), charcoal garden stone (#4A4A47) and moss (#6E7A4C), with exactly one deep-indigo textile accent (#2C3A5C); diffuse daylight, deep still shadows, generous emptiness (yohaku), minimal floating glass UI; Shippori Mincho for inscriptional labels, Zen Kaku Gothic New for the interface — a different designer entirely from every warm-Mediterranean, mosaic or terracotta piece in the library.
